criteria.title: Green Infrastructure
criteria.description: Ensure that the site complies with the relevant master plan/local development plans and guidelines.

children.description: Ensure that the site plan is in conformity with the development plan/master plan/Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) guidelines. This should comply with the provisions of eco-sensitive zone regulations, coastal zone regulations, heritage areas (identified in the master plan or issued separately as specific guidelines), waterbody zones (in such zones, no construction is permitted in the waterspread and buffer belt of minimum 30m around the full tank level), various hazardprone area regulations, and others if the site falls under any such area. Furthermore, any other relevant legal approval pertaining to the project for clearance from the necessary government authority has to be compliant.
Provision for mature trees on site.
Alternative 1: There are no existing mature trees on site.
Alternative 2: Demonstrate that the project team implements tree preservation measures as per the alternatives mentioned below:
Ensure that no exsiting mature tree on-site is cut.
Transplant existing mature trees (if applicable) within the site and ensure that they survive.
Plant three trees for every one tree cut of the same native/naturalized species.
Adopt any combination of the previously mentioned alternatives.

Ensure that a minimum of one tree for every 80m2 of site area (within GRIHA project boundary) is planted and maintained in order to increase vegetation on the site. The existing preserved mature trees within the site premises should be considered in the calculation.
Ensure that per capita gross area benchmark is between 5-10 sqm per capita.

Ensure that the average distance to at least five basic public amenities/services as per the building typology (defined in Appendix 1A, Table 1.1A and 1.2A, Volume 2) from the main entrance of the project is less than the GRIHA base case5 as per Table 1.2c.
Adopt any one strategy from the list, as given below, to promote sustainable transportation within the site premises.
Strategy 1: Provide at least four designated parking spaces for informal modes of transport within the site premises.

Strategy 2: Non-motorized transport/E vehicles
 - Part A: Provide E-vehicle parking facility for at least 5% of the total four-wheeler parking space along with charging facility for E-vehicles and adequate signage. 
 - Part B: Additionally provide designated vehicular tracks for NMT vehicles for site areas >50,000 m2.

Strategy 3: Provide bicycle users with at least 5% of the total four-wheeler parking space designated to them. Along with one changing room, shower, and locker per 100 bicycle parking spaces, within the site premises with adequate signage.

2 (with at least 1 passive strategy)
3 (with at least 2 passive strategies)
5 (with at least 3 passive strategies)

criteria.title: Air and Soil Pollution Control
criteria.description: Minimize air and soil pollution due to construction activities.

children.description: Adopt at least six measures to minimize air and soil pollution during construction, with the first three strategies being mandatory.
Provide 3m high continuous barricading along the site boundary/virtual boundary
Provide wheel washing facility/gravel bed at all vehicular entrances and exits of the site
Ensure DG sets have an exhaust with stack height of at least 2m from the top of the generator with a cowl
Ensure DGs are in compliance with CPCB norms
Implement a spill prevention plan for storage of diesel, admixtures, curing compounds, bitumen, and other hazardous materials
Ensure that fine aggregate, excavated earth, and other construction materials with a tendency to get airborne are covered or are sprinkled regularly with non-potable water.
Ensure sprinkling of water on unpaved pathways on the site with non-potable water.
Limit the speed of vehicular movement on-site to 10km/h.
Ensure that vehicles carrying waste materials out of the site are covered.

Ensure that the soil erosion channels are constructed and they are connected to a sedimentation tank in order to reduce movement of soil outside the site throughout the construction phase of the project.

criteria.title: Topsoil Preservation
criteria.description: Ensure the preservation of available fertile soil on-site and avoid its degradation during the process of construction.

children.description: Select any one of the alternatives

Applicability check: If the topsoil present on-site before construction is not
fertile and cannot be made fertile through organic means, the project is exempt from
Appraisal 5.1.1.

Ensure that topsoil from disturbed areas on the site is preserved, stabilized, and its fertility is maintained throughout the construction period. Additionally, ensure that 100% of the soil requirement for landscaping including roof garden(s) is met through this preserved soil.

criteria.title: Construction Management Practices
criteria.description: Ensure adoption of good management practices on-site during the construction phase.

children.description: Adopt construction management practices (e.g., stacking and storage of construction materials at different stages of construction) and ensure safe disposal of waste generated during construction.

Adopt at least two strategies from the list, as given below, to minimize water consumption during construction, with the first strategy being mandatory.
 • Use gunny bags, ponding technique, or curing compound.
 • Meter and monitor the consumption of water during construction.
 • Use water-reducing admixtures in concrete mix.
 • Use treated wastewater and/or captured storm water.

criteria.title: Energy Optimization
criteria.description: Improve energy efficiency by enhancing envelope performance and reduce energy consumption

children.description: Ensure that the project demonstrates compliance with the mandatory requirements of ECBC 2017 as per Table 7.5c, Details to Appraisals, Volume 3.
Ensure that the heat gain through the building envelope is below the GRIHA threshold for peak heat gain as per Table 7.1c
Demonstrate that 100% of exterior lighting fixtures (lamp+ballast) meet the luminous efficacy of 80lm/W
Ensure that the project demonstrates reduction (0% ≤ x < 10%) from the GRIHA benchmark for EPI as per Table 7.2c.
Additional EPI reduction will be awarded as per Table 7.3c
Ensure that the equipment installed within the project (whichever applicable as per Table 7.4c) is either BEE star lablled or of equal performance.
Star Labelled
3 Stars and above

criteria.description: Promote the use of renewable energy thereby, reduce project's dependency on fuels derived from conventional sources

children.description: Alternatives
Alt2: Demonstrate that 100% of the annual energy consumption of internal artificial lighting HVAC, and domestic hot water systems is offset through off-site RE systems.

criteria.title: Low ODP And GWP Materials
criteria.description:
Ensure the use of materials with low GWP and ODP in building
insulation, HVAC, refrigeration equipment, and firefighting systems.

children.description: Ensure that all the insulation used in the building envelope and for HVAC systems are CFC and HCFC free.
Ensure that the refrigerant used in the HVAC systems and refrigeration equipment is CFC and HCFC free.
Ensure that the fire suppression systems and fire extinguishers installed in the project are halon free.
Ensure that all the insulation used in the building envelope and for HVAC systems; refrigerant used in the HVAC systems and refrigeration equipment are HFC free.

criteria.title: Visual Comfort
criteria.description: Ensure visual comfort (daylight and artificial lighting) is provided through integration of active and passive design measure.

children.description: Demonstrate mean DA or UDI compliance as per Alternative 1 or Alternative 2.
Alternative - 1
Demonstrate through simulation that mean DA requirement (<3000lux) is met for 100% of the annual analysis hours for 100% of the regularly occupied areas.
Demonstrate through simulation that mean DA requirement (>300lux) is met for the 25% annual hours for 100% of the regularly occupied areas.
Demonstrate through simulation that mean DA requirement (>300lux) is met for the following annual hours for 100% of the regularly occupied areas.
Alternative - 2
Ensure that WWR does not exceed 60% and the vertical fenestration complies with minimum visual light transmittance (VLT) of 0.27.
Choose Any One of the Following
Ensure that the project meets the SHGC compliance as per Table 10.2c.
Ensure that the project meets the weighted average facade SHGC for each orientation as per Table 10.2c requirements.
Use Tables 9 and 10 of SP 41 to design the shading device for all the windows.

Conduct solar path analysis for all regularly occupied spaces (both conditioned and non-conditioned) to ensure that the windows are completely shaded for the duration between 0900 hours on March 15 to 1500 hours on September 15.
Use any combination of the above strategies to show compliance for 100% of the fenestrations.

Ensure that the skylight roof ratio (SRR) does not exceed 5% and SHGC for skylights13 does not exceed 0.35.
Only transparent, semi-transparent, or translucent horizontal fenestrations installed for the purposes of daylighting and/or views are considered skylights.14

Ensure that all regularly occupied spaces meet or exceed illuminance level between 100lux and 2000lux for the minimum 40% of floor area for 90% of the potential daylight time in a year. UDI compliance must be demonstrated through simulation using a validated software.

Ensure that all regularly occupied spaces meet or exceed illuminance level between 100lux and 2000lux for the minimum of following floor area for 90% of the potential daylight time in a year. UDI compliance must be demonstrated through simulation using a validated software.

Artificial lighting design to fall within limits (lower and higher range limits) as
recommended space/task-specific lighting levels as per National Building Code (NBC)
201616 and to meet a minimum uniformity ratio of 0.4.

criteria.title: Thermal & Acoustic Comfort
criteria.description: Ensure that occupants of the building are thermally and acoustically comfortable

children.description: Demonstrate that the project meets the thermal comfort requirements for all regularly occupied spaces as specified below (Table 11.1c)

Demonstrate that acoustic comfort requirements are met for all regularly occupied spaces in the building as per 11.1.2 A and B

Part A        
Measure outdoor noise levels and adopt at least three (of five) strategies in accordance with NBC 2016, Part8, Section4 if the average outdoor noise level is above 70dBA for conditioned buildings with sealed windows and 60dBA for naturally ventilated buildings and mixed mode buildings

Part B        
Demonstrate that indoor noise levels are within acceptable limits as per NBC 2016, Part 8, Section 4 and key noise sources on-site (DG, chillar plant etc) have sufficient acoustic insulation as per NBC 2016

criteria.description: Ensures design and monitoring of ventilation systems such that IAQ meets the minimum requirements

children.description: If the project comprises spaces with operable windows, then such spaces are exempted from Appraisals 12.1.1 and 12.1.2
The criteria is applicable in the project
The criteria is not applicable in the project
Ensure that the minimum requirements of CPCB (National Ambient Air Quality Standards [NAAQS]) for assessing the quality of fresh air are fulfilled.

Ensure that the minimum requirements of ASHRAE Standard 62.1-2010, Sections 4-7, Ventilation for Acceptable Indoor Air Quality (with errata), or NBC 2016, Volume 2, Part 8, Section 3, for quantity of fresh air are met.

Ensure continuous monitoring of CO, CO2, temperature, and RH levels such that they meet the permissible thresholds as per Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers (ISHRAE) standard 10001:2016, Table 6, for all habitable areas either at space level or at AHUs by installation of sensor(s) deployed with feedback system as per the alternatives mentioned in Table 12.1c and 12..2c
Sensors

1 sensor of space >=30sqm and <=100sqm

Install one sensor at each AHU (return air duct)
Install digital display showing monitored values for CO, CO2, temperature, and RH at each floor level (common areas) with permissible thresholds (12.2c) and clear visibility for all occupants
Ensure that all interior wall and ceiling finishes (including, but not limited to, primers and paints) have low volatile organic compound (VOC) content as per Table 12.3c and are lead-free
Ensure that all adhesives and sealants used have low VOC content as per Tables 12.4c and 12.5c and that interior composite wood products do not have urea-formaldehyde as a bonding resin
Ensure improved IAQ by adopting a minimum of three strategies from Table 12.6c.

criteria.title: Waste Management - Post Occupancy
criteria.description: Demonstrate compliance with all relevant government-notified waste management rules.

children.description: All the entities listed in Table 17.1c are considered bulk consumers and they need to mandatorily comply with the designated waste management rules.

Provide infrastructure (multi-coloured waste bins/different refuse chutes to store e-waste, biomedical waste, organic waste, plastic waste, paper waste, and other inorganic solid waste) for building occupants to ensure segregation of waste at the source.

Ensure that dedicated, segregated, and hygienic storage spaces are provided within the project site (for different types of waste listed in Appraisal 17.1.2) before treatment/recycling.

Provide contractual tie-ups with waste recyclers for safe handling and recycling of all types of inorganic waste generated on site. Also, ensure that 100% of recyclable waste is recovered/diverted (by means of recycling/processing through dedicated recyclers) and other inorganic waste (apart from recyclable waste) should be disposed off through authorized vendors.

criteria.title: Organic Waste Management
criteria.description: Divert organic waste from landfill sites by adopting strategies for treating ir and thereby mitigating its adverse effects on the surrounding environement.

children.description: Ensure that the organic waste generated onsite from the building (as per Criterion 17) and landscape areas is quantified, and adopt strategies to treat 100% organic waste onsite/offsite to convert it into usable resources (manure, biogas, etc.).

criteria.title: Utilization of Alternative Materials in Building
criteria.description: Encourage use of alternative materials, which minimize the detrimental impact of construction on environment by conserving natural resources, further minimizing the use of virgin materials and diverting usable (as per industry standards) wastes from the landfills to the construction industry

children.description: Ensure minimum replacement of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) recommended waste materials by weight of cement used in structural concrete.
Ensure minimum 5% replacement of natural aggregate with recycled concrete aggregate (RCA)/recycled aggregate (RA) by weight of that category of aggregate in structural concrete.

Ensure that all internal and external, load-bearing, non-load-bearing and partition walls are constructed with any, or combination of the below listed, alternative materials:

-Concrete blocks (hollow, solid, or AAC) with minimum 40% fly ash content by weight 
-Hollow clay blocks
-Adobe bricks/stabilized adobe/CSEB/stabilized mud blocks
-Rammed earth walls
-Stones from India (not including stone cladding)
-Bamboo/any other rapidly renewable material (not including bamboo cladding)
- Monolithic concrete wall demonstrating minimum 20% replacement of OPC with BIS recommended waste material by weight of cement
-C&D waste blocks demonstrating minimum 30% C&D waste material by weight
-Dry walls/boards with minimum 5% recycled content by weight
Cement & Mortart Applicability Check
Applicability: Projects where both cement mortar and plaster have not been used are exempted from Appraisals 19.1.4
Ensure minimum 30% replacement of OPC with BIS recommended waste by weight of cement used in masonry mortar and plaster.

criteria.description: Encourage the project to optimize construction product consumption efficiency by selecting low GWP (kgCO2eq) products through LCA of the building.

Demonstrate reduction in the GWP value of the building interiors and finishes as per the LCA benchmarks mentioned in Table 20.2c.

criteria.title: Alternative Materials for External Site Development
criteria.description: Substitute conventional materials used for external site development with alternative materials, in order to reduce pressure on both mining for virgin materials and landfills required for the disposal of waste material.

children.description:
Ensure that at least 70% of all roads and vehicular pathways within site premises are constructed with one, or any combination, of the following:
a. Bituminous road with minimum 6% plastic waste content by weight of bitumen
b. Cast in-situ cement concrete road with minimum 30% fly ash content by weight of total cementitious material
c. Concrete blocks with minimum 40% fly ash content by weight of block
d. Paver blocks containing minimum 10% C&D waste content by weight of block
e. Stones from India
f. Any other product with minimum 10% recycled content by weight.

Ensure that 100% of the pavement/footpath including kerb stone constructed on-site are constructed with one, or any combination, of the following:
a. Bituminous road with minimum 6% plastic waste content by weight of bitumen
b. Cast in-situ cement concrete road with minimum 30% fly ash content by weight of total cementitious material
c. Concrete blocks with minimum 40% fly ash content by weight of block
d. Paver blocks containing minimum 10% C&D waste content by weight of block
e. Stones from India
f. Any other product with minimum 10% recycled content by weight.

10 years ≥ x > 8 years

criteria.title: Safety and Sanitation for Construction Workers
criteria.description: Ensure safe, healthy, and hygienic working and living conditions for construction workers involved in the project.

children.description:
Ensure compliance with the requirements of NBC 2016 for all of the following:
- Part 1: Provision of necessary safety equipment and safety measures for construction workers.
- Part 2: Provision of clean drinking water, hygienic working and living conditions, and sanitation facilities for the workers.
- Part 3: Provision of crèche facility for children of construction workers in case their families are allowed to work/live at the construction site.
Adopt one alternative out of the following for the construction workers on-site.
Alternative 1: Provide a grocery store/canteen within the site premises and/or labour accommodation.
Alternative 2: Organize at least two events during the entire construction phase to create environmental awareness among the construction workers.

criteria.title: Universal Accessibility
criteria.description: Encourage the adoption of measure that make the built environment barrier free and accessible to all, including people with disabilities and elderly persons.

children.description: Ensure that the project complies with the provisions of Harmonised Guidelines and Space Standards for Barrier Free Built Environment for Persons with Disability and Elderly Persons, 2016

criteria.title: Dedicated Facilities for Service Staff

children.description: Ensure the provision of dedicated room(s) for resting for service staff on-site.
Ensure the provision of toilets on-site for service staff as per fixtures mentioned in NBC 2016, Volume 2, Part 9, Section 2, Clause 4.2 (refer to Table 25.1c, Volume 6)

criteria.title: Positive Social Impact
criteria.description: Create a healthy environment by ensuring adoption of measures for clean indoor and outdoor air and raising environmental awareness amongst building occupants and the community.

children.description: On-site: Ensure that the project adopts one measure on-site to create environmental awareness amongst its occupants and visitors.
Adopt one alternative out of the following for environmental awareness post occupancy:
Alternative 1 (On-site): Ensure that the project adopts an additional (to 26.1.1.) measure for occupants and visitors to create environmental awareness.
Alternative 2 (Off-site): Ensure that the project conducts a minimum of 2 programmes in a year to create environmental awareness amongst general masses.
Demonstrate that the project team has implemented tobacco smoke control measures in case of air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned buildings as per the alternatives mentioned below:
Alternative 1: Ensure that tobacco smoking is prohibited within the site premises.

Alternative 2: Ensure that designated smoking zone(s) is provided and the smoke is managed within a controlled environment (in case of air-conditioned buildings). Additionally, smoking must be prohibited in public spaces.
Ensure that tobacco smoking is prohibited on-site during the entire construction phase.
Ensure that the per capita availability of green spaces for the project site is more than GRIHA benchmark of minimum 9 sqm. of green space per capita.

criteria.description: Ensure that all electro-mechanical systems and their components are designed and installed accroding to the operational requirements of the owner.

children.description: Ensure that third-party commissioning is conducted for the systems mentioned in Table 27.1c

criteria.title: Smart Metering and Monitoring
criteria.description: Promote smart metering and monitoring of energy and water consumption of the project to anlayse performance

children.description: Demonstrate compliance with the following source metering requirements as mentioned in Table 28.1c
Demonstrate compliance with the following extended metering requirements as mentioned in Table 28.2c
Energy
Water

Ensure installation of smart metering systems (refer Table 28.3c) which are capable of tracking energy and water consumption through a web-hosted portal for all meters, as mentioned in Appraisal 28.1.1

All smart metering and monitoring systems should be capable of the following:
- Hourly data reporting on near realtime (no more than 15-min delay)
- Energy mix breakdown and consumption patterns
- Water consumption patterns from various sources
- Ability to set energy and water consumption targets, alarms, and pricing
- Ability to compare historical trends and benchmark data
- Real-time monitoring with user interface that operates even on mobile devices.
Installation of one-way communicable system
Installation of two-way communicable system
Ensure sharing of monthly energy and water consumption data of the project by connecting with the GRIHA Online Benchmarking platform for 5 years.
